question.leadin: Identify these African countries going through difficult political times.
question.text: This country's 2005 elections were delayed until 2010, when Laurent Gbagbo (LAR-rent BAG-bow) refused to accept his defeat to Alassane Ouattara (ah-lah-SAH-nay wah-TAR-ah).
question.answerHtml: Republic of Côte d'Ivoire [or Republique de Côte d'Ivoire; or Ivory Coast]
question.clue: A soccer match held in this country's rebel-controlled city of Bouake eased tensions during its civil war fought between supporters of Guillaume Soro and Laurent Gbagbo ("lo-RAWN guh-BAG-bo").

swap.text: Not to be accused of lacking attention to detail, Amin also clarified that he was the conqueror of this country "in Particular". Idi Amin brutally ruled this country for most of the 1970s, during which he expelled all Asians from it.
swap.clue: In 1972, the Jews and Asians were expelled from this country, in which several hostages were rescued in a raid on Entebbe.

question.leadin: Stories of this ruler's largesse include a legend that he built a mosque every Friday during one of his travels.
question.text: Name this 14th century Mansa of the Mali Empire, best known for a legendary hajj.
question.clue: The architect Abu Isaq al Saheli was commissioned by this ruler to build the Djinguereber mosque.

swap.text: This African nation, which also suffers from hyperinflation, is led by Robert Mugabe. To "counter" inflation, this nation removed 10 zeros from its currency in 2008, making 10 billion dollars equal to one.
swap.clue: It's not Kenya, but British intervention in this country led to the Lancaster House agreement that ended Ian Smith's white minority rule.

question.text: This raid, which led to the Second Boer War, was supposed to trigger an uprising of the British Uitlanders who held a diminutive status in the Transvaal Republic.
question.clue: Although this event was ultimately a failure, as it intended to trigger an uprising among the Uitlanders ] in Transvaal, it was a major cause of the Second Boer War.

swap.leadin: Garnet Wolseley led an expedition to relieve a siege in this present-day country, where Charles Gordon was killed.
swap.text: Name this country, where Muhammed Ahmed claimed to be the Mahdi and led a rebellion against Anglo-Egyptian rule.
swap.clue: One referendum run by this country used images of clasped and unclasped hands due to widespread illiteracy, and a key group in this country, the National Islamic Front, was founded by Hassan al-Turabi.

question.leadin: This empire secured power after defeating the Denkyira kingdom made up of the Akan people.
question.text: Name this empire ruled by figures such as King Osei Tutu, whose capital was located at the city of Kumasi.
question.clue: Queen Yaa Asantewaa of this empire started a war after Frederick Hodgson demanded that he sit on a certain sacred object.

swap.leadin: This war included two invasions of a neighboring country's Shaba province.
swap.text: Name this lengthy war in which the communist MPLA defeated its rival UNITA.
swap.clue: Allegations that an election during this war was rigged caused the 1992 Halloween Massacre, which killed many Bakongo and Ovimbundu people.

question.leadin: A locally produced model of an Israeli submachine gun, nicknamed the "Rhuzi," was used by this country's Selous Scouts against organizations like ZAPU and ZANU.
question.text: Name this country where Ian Smith led a white minority government until 1979, when this nation became Zimbabwe.
question.clue: After 1970 the only time the Union Flag was flown in this country officially was Pioneers' Day.

swap.text: From trade with the Congolese, the Portuguese acquired ivory oliphants. The Portuguese also commissioned the Sapi of this modern-day country to create ivory salt cellars, one of which is displayed by the Met.
swap.clue: This country used IMF funds to pay South African mercenary firm Executive Outcomes to terrorize its citizens.

question.leadin: A politician from this country, Hassan Al-Turabi, was nearly karate-chopped to death by an exiled black belt master.
question.text: Name this African country once ruled by Omar Al-Bashir. This country's southern portion gained independence in 2011 following a civil war against the National Islamic Front.
question.answerHtml: Republic of the Sudan [or North Sudan; reject “South Sudan”]
question.clue: The northern part of this nation embraced Islam, while the southern portion embraced the animist {AHN-I-MIST} and Christian religions.

swap.leadin: The British opposed the Portuguese Pink Map because it would interfere with this project.
swap.text: Name this project that was envisioned by a political cartoon showing Cecil Rhodes straddling Africa, holding a telegraph line in his hands. This railway project intended to connect British colonies in Africa from north to south.
swap.clue: Land needed for this project was explored by the Pioneer Column after it was acquired in the Rudd Concession, which was obtained from King Lobengula.

question.text: Other Nigerian military leaders during the war included this general, who later took over Nigeria in a 1976 coup, although he transitioned the country back to democracy. He was so popular that he was also Nigeria's democratically elected president from 1999 to 2007.

swap.text: This city, whose name means "city of a thousand" is the capital of Madagascar.
swap.clue: One woman who ruled from this city applied a trial by ordeal involving eating toxic tangena nuts en masse.

question.leadin: According to Abd al-Sadi's Tarikh al-Sudan, this emperor drowned while crossing the Niger River.
question.text: Name this emperor, who claimed to be able to turn himself into a vulture and make his armies invisible. He founded an empire whose capital city was Gao.
question.clue: Notable military efforts he led include an attack against Mossi raiders, a victory in Massina, and his successful seven year siege of Jenne.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about cities in the Middle East that saw major protests in 2011.
swap.text: This city, the third most populous in Libya, was threatened with a massacre when the United States and other countries intervened militarily.
swap.clue: Much of the fighting in Libya has centered on this third most populous city, which is located 130 miles east of Tripoli. It was the city that Muammar Qaddafi's forces were destroying when NATO intervened and where two American photojournalists were killed by mortars.

question.leadin: Agostinho Neto took over control of this organization in 1962.
question.text: Identify this Cuban-backed faction agitating for Angolan independence, a rival of groups like the FLNA and UNITA.
question.clue: This socialist party led by the poet Agostinho Neto, which opposed UNITA in a decades-long civil war following his country's independence.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Leo Wolpert's favorite breakaway state, Katanga.
swap.text: When Patrice Lumumba became Congo's prime minister in 1960, this founder of the Belgian-backed CONAKAT party and president of Katanga declared the province's secession.
swap.clue: The main crisis of Lumumba's short time in office was the independence movement in the southern mineral-rich province of Katanga, which had Belgian backing. This man led that briefly-independent republic.

question.leadin: After emerging from the poolside bathroom where he was hiding, this leader recited the first surah of the Quran to pacify the soldiers trying to overthrow him during his 42nd birthday party.
question.text: Name this member of the 'Alawi dynasty, who convinced treasonous pilots to stop shooting his plane by radioing, "The tyrant is dead!" This king, who used the secret Tazmamart prison during his country's Years of Lead, also authorized the Green March to expel Spain from Western Sahara.
question.answerHtml: Hassan II [accept Mawlay al-Hassan bin Mohammed bin Yusef al-Alawi; prompt on just Hassan]

swap.text: Mobutu called in Soviets in an attempt to stop this leader of the CONAKAT party from creating an independent nation out of the copper-rich province of Katanga.
swap.clue: This leader of the secessionist state of feuded with both Lumumba and Joseph Kasavubu. After the UN invasion of he fled to .
